newsitem.title: LATVIA: New Latvian government wins parliament backing.
newsitem.headline: New Latvian government wins parliament backing.

text.p: New Latvian Prime Minister Guntar Krasts, who has pledged to pursue the former Soviet state's reforms and stick to a tough budget policy, was formally voted into power by parliament on Thursday.
Krasts leads a six-party coalition that ranges from nationalists to left-of-centre parties.
He got the backing of 73 MPs in the 100-seat parliament while 13 voted against, the parliament press office said. He had been expected to win the vote as his coalition has 67 seats.
Krasts, economy minister in the previous government, said he would stick to the strict monetary and budget policies of former prime minister Andris Shkele.
"Last year's budget project will not change," Krasts told parliament.
Shkele, a tough businessman without party affiliation, vowed to end Latvia's economic crisis when he took office in 1995.
He last year passed a balanced 1997 budget to cut spending and drive down interest rates, as the key plank of his plans.
But Shkele was forced to step down after 18 months in office after rowing with the leading coalition parties.
Local commentators say Krasts may have trouble keeping budget discipline and fulfilling his plans, given a wide-ranging coalition which may want to pull in different directions.
Krasts' programme also calls for speeding reforms and making sure Latvia begins early talks on European Union (EU) entry.
Of the Baltic states, only Estonia was recommended by the European Commission to begin early membership talks.
But Latvia and third Baltic state Lithuania hope to persuade EU leaders to accept them for entry talks at a summit in December, where the final decision on new entrants will be made.
